task: Review existing Lapis settings storage and its accessibility to supervised agents

source.scope_note: Read-only source review; no user settings or unrelated dirty work were modified. A focused ignored build artifact was produced.

checks.command: sindexer search . "settings persistence configuration storage restore QSettings workspace" --limit 5
checks.result: Located KeyMap, workspace restore, geometry persistence, and architecture references.
Focused keymap suite passed, including atomic write-back, unknown-key preservation, rollback, validation, and external replacement hot reload.

checks.command: runtime inventory of active packaged lapis.json, workspace.json, and window.json plus desktop process environment filtering
checks.result: Active config is under ~/.lapis; workspace and geometry are private mode-0600 runtime JSON. The running desktop exposes neither LAPIS_HOME nor LAPIS_CONFIG.

findings: lapis.json is already a small JSON document with a version key, but read paths do not enforce that version and no JSON Schema is shipped.
The GUI writes atomically, preserves unknown JSON fields, rolls back failed mutations, diagnoses invalid fields, and reloads replacement writes from external editors or agents after a 150 ms settle.

Active packaged settings, agent registry, and window geometry are intentionally split across lapis.json, runtime/workspace.json, and runtime/window.json; the latter two are private machine-local state.

Supervised local agents do not inherit a pointer to the active config. A packaged agent whose working directory is this checkout would find the committed default ./lapis.json rather than the active ~/.lapis/lapis.json.
Direct agent edits have no advisory lock or compare-and-swap generation, so concurrent UI and agent read-modify-write cycles can lose updates even though each write is atomic.
Agents have no machine-readable validation or diagnostics surface; invalid values fall back in the GUI and appear only as GUI diagnostic text.
Remote SSH agents have no local settings-access contract; blindly forwarding the local config path would be a separate security and consistency decision.
recommendation: Keep JSON and add a local self-describing contract rather than changing formats: inject the active LAPIS_CONFIG/LAPIS_HOME into local agent environments, ship a Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema with additionalProperties true, and provide a small JSON CLI for path/schema/validate/read/write that shares the same lock and validation. Before implementation, decide version enforcement and conflict behavior explicitly.
non_claims: This review did not modify or reload the user's active settings.
The focused keymap suite does not requalify the full desktop, workspace, iOS, or packaging stacks.
No settings CLI, schema, environment injection, or concurrency protocol was implemented.
Remote agent settings access and nested Lapis behavior remain undesigned.
